clue.text: Comfortable, some of us, on £50

blocks.note: a group of people including the speaker
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign's letter; 'on' just places it after
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Some of us feel comfortably off with fifty pounds in our pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: The £50 splits in two: the pound sign is L and the 50 is another L. Theme: the Bank of England £50 note carries Turing, and once carried Boulton and Watt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well off is to be comfortable financially, and 'well' alone also describes someone at ease or in good health.

clue.text: Come to author you shouldn't have put in the middle division

indicators.note: something put in the middle sits inside another word, splitting it in two

blocks.note: to come to is to regain consciousness, to wake
to author a piece is to pen it
what you say on receiving a gift, i.e. thanks; TA is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for writing to an author and placing a remark in the middle section of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN and TA go together into the middle of WAKE. 'You shouldn't have!' is the polite gasp at a present, so it stands for thanks, TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A wapentake was an old subdivision of a shire in the Danelaw counties, such as the Yorkshire Ridings.

clue.text: Angry 6 unlikely to go unnoticed

indicators.note: an angry thing is agitated and stirred up, so the letters get thrown about

blocks.note: the answer to 6 Down

explanation.surface: An angry stare is hard to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something large is big and conspicuous, so it is hard to overlook.

clue.text: Maths whizz working out N from deviation

indicators.note: working something out of a word is easing it out, taking it away

blocks.note: the letter to be removed
a turning is a deviation from a straight course

explanation.surface: A mathematician calculates a figure from a statistical deviation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' looks like doing sums, which suits the maths whizz, but it means removing. Take the first N out of TURNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing was the mathematician and codebreaker who now appears on the Bank of England £50 note.

clue.text: Berners-Lee's decision, his last, on the dot

indicators.note: the last of a name is its final letter alone

blocks.note: a decision that is Tim Berners-Lee's to make is 'up to Tim'
his refers to Berners-Lee, whose surname ends in E

explanation.surface: The inventor of the web makes a punctual decision.
explanation.walkthrough: A choice that belongs to someone is 'up to' them, so Tim Berners-Lee's decision is up to Tim; then add the final letter of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to time means punctual, arriving exactly at the appointed moment, which is what on the dot means.

clue.text: Pass kid, not excited by present

indicators.note: excited things are stirred into motion, so these letters get jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the present moment is now

explanation.surface: A child is passed a present but isn't excited by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a verb about handing the kid something; it is the quiz-show word for declining to answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a quiz, saying 'pass' is the same as admitting you have no answer.

clue.text: 7 Down flourishes dazzle with brilliance

indicators.note: a flourish is an extravagant waving about, which shakes these letters into new order

blocks.note: the answer to 7 Down

explanation.surface: Kingly flourishes dazzle onlookers with their brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to shine with a harsh, dazzling light.

clue.text: Inlet's mouth submerged by river close to sea

definitions.text: Inlet's mouth submerged by river close to sea

indicators.note: a mouth is an opening, so only the opening letter is kept
the close of a word is its ending, so only its final letter is kept
something submerged is surrounded, so one piece sits inside the others

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
the opening letter of inlet
the final letter of sea

explanation.surface: The mouth of an inlet has been drowned by a river where it nears the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a ria forms when rising sea floods a river valley near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long coastal inlet made by the sea drowning the lower part of a river valley.

clue.text: 23 all round, on His Majesty!

definitions.note: adjective: of or befitting a king

indicators.note: turning all the way round makes the word face the other direction

blocks.note: the answer to 23 Down

explanation.surface: A round of drinks is ordered for everyone and put on the King's tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' tempts as a round of beers to go with the lager, but 'all round' turns the word about.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, relating to or fit for a monarch such as His Majesty.

clue.text: Area measures perhaps represented, but as outlines

indicators.note: re-presented means set out again in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Measurements of area are depicted only as outlines on a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the puzzle's key: RAPE, RIDING, WAPENTAKE and LATHE are all old county divisions, area measures of a kind. 'Perhaps' marks the definition as by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of area such as the square metre are absolute units, fixed standard measures; perhaps signals examples.

clue.text: English post boxes few and far between

blocks.note: to box in practice is to spar
E for English, coming post, i.e. after

explanation.surface: English post boxes are scarce in some places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post boxes' reads as a pillar box; split it: 'post' means after, and 'boxes' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, which is exactly what few and far between describes.

clue.text: Superheroine born in western Arabian state

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born
at and in both indicate location
W is the abbreviation for west
Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A comic-book heroine was born in the west of an Arabian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Batwoman is a DC Comics heroine, a female counterpart to Batman.

clue.text: Mind-blowing leading man stunned this lady!

indicators.note: to blow something is to lose it, so those letters go missing
something stunned is knocked senseless and reeling, so the remaining letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters M, I, N and D are the ones removed
the letters from which the removal is made

explanation.surface: A woman is stunned by a dazzling leading man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind-blowing' reads as one adjective; split it, so MIND is lost from LEADING MAN and the six letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's given name, and the exclamation presents the answer as the lady herself.

clue.text: Quartet of duos rock: it's better dishabille!

indicators.note: dishabille is a state of undress, so each word loses its outer covering of letters

blocks.note: rock stripped of its first and last letters
it's stripped of its first and last letters
better stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A double quartet decides that rock music sounds better performed half-dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dishabille, from French, means being only partly clothed; here each of the three words sheds its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Four pairs make eight, and an octette is a group of eight musicians, the variant spelling of octet.

clue.text: Preposterously, in one paradox, a cultivated source of oil; in another, a perfect source of vinegar

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their join
preposterous literally means before-behind, back to front, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the end of one and start of paradox, read in the clue's order
a second instance: the same four letters run forwards across the end of another and through a perfect

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing on paradoxes, set out like a riddle about oil and vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings, each with its own hidden version: backwards in 'one paradox', forwards in 'another, a perfect'. Oilseed rape is the yellow field crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Rape is the oilseed crop grown for oil, and rape is also the residue of grape skins and stalks used in making vinegar.

clue.text: Charged criminal — no longer top, showing effects of inaction

indicators.note: having no top any more means the first letter has been taken off

blocks.note: bent is slang for dishonest or criminal
metal left unused corrodes

explanation.surface: A charged criminal, no longer a top dog, shows the effects of idle time inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like a criminal being charged by police; it means given responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To be entrusted with something is to be charged with it, given it as a duty or responsibility.

clue.text: Karma that tree's exudation will feed rail

indicators.note: feeding something in means inserting it inside another word

blocks.note: karma is destiny shaped by one's deeds, i.e. fate
ulmin is a brown substance exuded by elm trees

explanation.surface: A belief that sap from a tree will nourish a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a fence; it is the verb meaning to rant. Ulmin is an obscure word, a brown substance from elm bark.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain or protest angrily, and to fulminate is to denounce someone vehemently.

clue.text: Its binding method reversed by lab procedure

indicators.note: binding something means wrapping round it, so one part encloses the other
turned to face the other way, the letters run from end to start

blocks.note: read as the plural of it: two of them
an art is a skill or technique, a way of doing something
on and by both mean beside, as in a house on or by the river

explanation.surface: A procedure in the lab undoes its own method of binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' is not the possessive: read it as a plural, two ITs, which wrap ART before the lot is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Titration is a chemistry lab technique for measuring concentration by adding a reagent until a reaction completes.

clue.text: Frost's opening, uplifting new line very much traveled by?

definitions.text: Frost's opening, uplifting new line very much traveled by?

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter is kept
in a down clue lifting up makes the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first letter of Frost
N is the abbreviation for new
a row is a line of things
too means excessively, very much

explanation.surface: Robert Frost's famous poem opens by lifting up a new line about a road that is much travelled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Frost's 'The Road Not Taken' chose the one 'less traveled by', so a path very much traveled by is footworn.
explanation.definitionFit: Footworn describes a path worn down by the feet of many walkers, i.e. heavily used.

clue.text: Sign by point in Gardens their partners maintain

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Kew Gardens is the botanic garden in south-west London
PT is the abbreviation for point
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A notice beside a viewpoint in a public garden that the partners help maintain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintain' looks like garden upkeep; it means keeping someone financially. 'By' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept women are mistresses financially supported, or maintained, by their lovers.

clue.text: Such power, picking something up

indicators.note: picking up a signal is hearing it, so the word goes by its sound

blocks.note: what can mean something, as in 'I'll tell you what'

explanation.surface: A device that draws a certain power when lifting things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone indicator is split around its object: 'picking ... up'. James Watt, with Matthew Boulton, appeared on the old £50 note.
explanation.definitionFit: The watt is the SI unit of power, so it is power of a particular kind.

clue.text: First of leading articles upon which much will turn

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the opening letter of leading
two articles, the indefinite and the definite

explanation.surface: The first of the leading newspaper articles, on which a great deal will depend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upon which much will turn' sounds like crucial, but is literal. A lathe was also an old division of Kent, fitting the area theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that spins a workpiece so it can be shaped, so things are turned on it.

clue.text: Engineer additional university cuts

indicators.note: cutting into something means entering it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a bolt-on is an extra, additional part
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An engineer is a further cut in university funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like the verb or an anagram signal; it is the definition, the Birmingham manufacturer who partnered James Watt.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Boulton was an eighteenth-century engineer and industrialist, partner of Watt in steam-engine manufacture.

clue.text: Fine carriage from Paris ejects European statesman

indicators.note: ejecting something throws it out, so the letter is removed

blocks.note: French for a fine bearing or deportment
E, the abbreviation for European, is the letter thrown out

explanation.surface: A smart French carriage throws out a European politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' reads as a coach, but here it is posture: bel air in French is fine deportment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was British Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007, a statesman.

clue.text: Account's initial level, having zilch in circulation

indicators.note: an initial is a word's first letter
having something means holding it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the first letter of account
level and flat both mean even
zilch means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: An account starts at an even balance, with nothing in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afloat is current or circulating, as rumours or money are said to be afloat.

clue.text: Drink rum, 2

indicators.note: rum here means odd or strange, so the letters come out peculiarly arranged

blocks.note: the answer to 2 Down

explanation.surface: Two drinks of rum are ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the spirit to drink; it is the British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common drink in pubs.

clue.text: Plant species found around Key West

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word encloses the others

blocks.note: a sort is a kind or species
ALT is a keyboard key
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A plant species is found growing around Key West in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key West' is the Florida island, but split it into two pieces, both of which go inside the word for species.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltwort is a plant of salt marshes and shores, used historically to make soda ash.

clue.text: Chap's nicking silver and grand dish

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, taking something into one's possession, so it goes inside

blocks.note: belonging to a chap: his
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
G for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A man steals silverware and a fine dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is the Scottish dish of offal, oatmeal and spices cooked in a sheep's stomach.

clue.text: Get the office of a senior clergyman

definitions.text: the office of a senior clergyman

blocks.note: first meaning: understand, as in 'I get it'

blocks.clueFragment: the office of a senior clergyman
blocks.note: second meaning: a bishop's diocese or seat

explanation.surface: Someone is sent to the office of a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the office' sounds like being called in by the boss; the first word is a meaning on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp it, and a see is the jurisdiction or seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Row fires doctor up

indicators.note: fires reads as a kiln firing clay held inside it, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: to doctor results is to rig them
a row is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: An argument fires up a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of 'fires up', but stands alone: in racing a jockey who is up is riding, as in 'Dettori up'. A riding was also a division of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing language a jockey said to be up is mounted on the horse, that is, riding it.

clue.text: Bird with a little experience in service

definitions.text: Bird with a little experience in service

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a bit of it, its first letter
in places that letter inside the other piece

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the Royal Navy, the senior service
the first letter of experience

explanation.surface: A young woman with a bit of experience serving in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a young woman, and a Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, so the whole clue defines it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A wren is a small songbird, and a Wren was a woman serving in the Royal Navy.
